2014_070_090214mtg.paragraph: Agenda packet for the Troy Board of Education regular meeting of September 2, 2014, held at 7:00 PM in the Services Building, 4420 Livernois. The business items carried three bond-program awards plus a tax matter: Troy High School additions and remodeling totaling $2,629,095.00, Boulan Park and Larson Middle Schools' additions and remodeling totaling $3,425,240.00, science supplies and equipment under Bid 9791 at $69,609.52, and amendment of Tax Rate Request Form L-4029 because operating Non-Homestead taxable values grew faster than inflation. Supporting material included probationary contracts for 26 new teachers, the appointment of Dan House as Assistant Principal of Troy High School, and enrollment of 12,571 students reported that morning.
2014_070_090214mtg.page:
**Meeting**
Regular meeting of the Troy Board of Education, September 2, 2014, 7:00 PM, Services Building, 4420 Livernois, Troy, MI 48098. District offices at 4400 Livernois, 248.823.4000; meetings cablecast on TS-TV Channel 19 (Comcast) and Channel 15 (WOW) and posted at vimeo.com/troyschools.

**Recognition**
- Sixteen Spring 2014 all-state athletes from Troy High and Athens High in boys and girls lacrosse, girls tennis, girls soccer, softball and boys track; biographies read by Mr. Jolly.
- Michigan Association of School Boards honors: Honor Board achievement and Standard of Excellence Award for the Board; Master Board Member Award and Advocacy Skill Specialty Award for President Nancy Philippart; MASB Level One Certification and Award of Merit for Secretary Karl Schmidt.
- ASBO International Certificate of Excellence in Financial Reporting for the CAFR for the fiscal year ended June 30, 2013, recognizing Assistant Superintendent for Business Services Mark Rajter; award letter of August 4, 2014 from Executive Director John D. Musso.
- Mission Moment: the Boulan Park Middle School LINKS program collected 1,022 personal letters, 2,790 items and cash totaling $142 for troops in Afghanistan; advisors Sandy Ford and Joe DeVault.

**Consent Agenda**
Minutes of the August 5, 2014 meeting, which recorded resolutions 14-087 through 14-094, all adopted 7 Yes / 0 No: consent items (July 8, 2014 minutes; Treasurer's Report for April and May 2014; copy paper); twelve new hires; a two-year probationary administrative contract for Kris Young as Director of Technology effective August 11, 2014; Section 105c Schools of Choice for 9th grade at International Academy East for 2015-2016; a $185,012.50 Smart Board award to VSC; an $883,950.00 Athens High School additions and remodeling award; a $90,140.00 food service equipment award to Stafford-Smith, Inc.; and MASB Delegate Assembly delegates for November 6-9, 2014. That meeting adjourned at 7:51 p.m.

**Personnel**
Probationary contracts recommended for 26 teachers for 2014-2015. Appointment of Dan House as Assistant Principal, Troy High School, effective September 3, 2014, on a two-year probationary administrative contract without tenure. Staffing update by Assistant Superintendent for Human Resources Jasen Witt: 44 new TSD teachers, 8 TSD graduates, 27 teachers with education beyond a bachelor's degree, 19 with five or more years of prior experience (7 of those with ten or more), and 185 total years of prior teaching experience as a group.

**Enrollment reported September 2, 2014**

| Level | September 3, 2013 | September 2, 2014 |
|---|---|---|
| Elementary total | 5,569 | 5,446 |
| Middle school total | 2,804 | 2,863 |
| High school total | 4,217 | 4,262 |
| Total students | 12,590 | 12,571 |

**Business awards**

| Item | Total |
|---|---|
| Troy High School additions and remodeling (Bid Package 5) | $2,629,095.00 |
| Boulan Park and Larson Middle Schools' additions and remodeling (Bid Package 6) | $3,425,240.00 |
| Science supplies and equipment, Bid 9791 | $69,609.52 |

Barton Malow reported a budget of $1,966,125 for Bid Package 5 with an overage of $662,970, and a budget of $2,814,450. for Bid Package 6 with an overage of $610,790.; both overages were recommended to be funded from construction contingency.

**Millage**
Because operating Non-Homestead taxable values grew greater than the rate of inflation, the Board was asked to amend the Tax Rate Request Form L-4029 and forward it to the appropriate tax jurisdictions; Michigan Department of Treasury Form 614 (Rev. 04-14) must be submitted on or before September 30, 2014.

**Other**
Bond projects update by Barton Malow Senior Project Manager Ron Curtis, and the unveiling of the OneTroy concept at the Opening Day staff gathering at Athens High School.
2014_070_090214mtg.verbose:
Board meeting agenda and supporting packet for the Troy School District Board of Education regular meeting of September 2, 2014, convened at 7:00 PM at the Services Building, 4420 Livernois, Troy, MI 48098. District administrative offices are at 4400 Livernois, Troy, Michigan 48098, 248.823.4000; meetings are cablecast on TS-TV Channel 19 (Comcast) and Channel 15 (WOW) every Monday and Wednesday at 2:00 and 9:00 p.m. when school is in session, and viewable at http://vimeo.com/troyschools.

RECOGNITION. Mr. Jolly read biographies of the Spring 2014 all-state athletes: Craig Bazin, Justice Bigelow, Nicholas Boynton, Jay Darish, Deepthi Devireddy, Jill Dougherty, Kyle Fietsam, David Fracassa, Amanda Harris, Sydney Heath, Lillian Liang, Ashley Messina, Sally Muller, Jacob Nelson, Kunal Tangri and Sarah Troccoli, representing Troy High School and Athens High School in boys and girls lacrosse, girls tennis, girls soccer, softball and boys track. Coaches named include Justin Suarez, Nate Reynolds, Brian Miska, Rob Holder, Todd Heugh, Tom Calnen, Scott Player and Brian Zawislak.

The Michigan Association of School Boards recognized the Troy Board of Education for its Honor Board achievement and a Standard of Excellence Award, President Nancy Philippart for the Master Board Member Award and the Advocacy Skill Specialty Award, and Secretary Karl Schmidt for MASB Level One Certification and the Award of Merit.

The Association of School Business Officials International awarded Troy School District its Certificate of Excellence in Financial Reporting for the Comprehensive Annual Financial Report for the fiscal year ended June 30, 2013, recognizing Mark Rajter, Assistant Superintendent for Business Services. The August 4, 2014 letter from Executive Director John D. Musso, CAE, RSBA, says the engraved plaque will be mailed in approximately 6-8 weeks. Review comments address page ix (duplicated debt information in the transmittal letter; GASBS 34:8 footnote 7; 2012 GAAFR pages 591-592), page 10 (construction in progress reported separately from land), disclosure of commitments in construction in progress (NCGA-I6:4j; 2012 GAAFR page 372), page 43 (basis of budgeting note; 2012 GAAFR page 580), pages 55-58 (remove an unneeded note), and pages 67-70 and 79 (principal property taxpayers and principal employers for the current fiscal period and the period nine years prior; GASBS 34:37; GASBS 44:19-20 & 34). GASB updates cover Statements No. 65 and No. 66 (March 2012), No. 67 and No. 68 (June 2012), No. 69 (January 2013), No. 70 (April 2013) and No. 71 (November 2013). The certificate is signed by Terrie S. Simmons, RSBA, CSBO, President, and John D. Musso. The award is sponsored by VALIC, which as of August 30, 2013 had more than $79 billion in total assets under management and managed plans for nearly 25,000 groups serving nearly 2 million plan participants. ASBO, founded in 1910, is at 11401 North Shore Drive, Reston, VA, 20190.

The TSD Mission Moment honored the Boulan Park Middle School LINKS program, which pairs students with different learning styles; an ASD class and its 8th grade mentors, led by Ms. Sandy Ford and Mr. Joe DeVault, collected 1,022 personal letters and 2,790 items such as snacks, bath items, gloves, CDs and games, plus cash totaling $142, assembled into care packages for troops in Afghanistan.

CONSENT AGENDA. Item A was the minutes of the August 5, 2014 Board of Education meeting at the Administration Building. President Philippart called that meeting to order at 7:00 p.m.; present were Board members Edmunds, Fleming, Hauff, Miletti, Schmidt and Underwood, Superintendent Machesky, administrators Birmingham, Dziatczak, Keeling, Machesky, Rajter and Witt, and approximately 8 members of the audience. Resolution 14-087 approved consent items A (minutes of the July 8, 2014 meeting), B (Treasurer's Report for April and May 2014) and C (copy paper), 7 Yes / 0 No. Resolution 14-088 approved new hires Kaitlin Bucchare, Ross Burdette, Aguib Diop, Lauren Field, Johnathan McNurlen, Tanya Myre, Laura Rasmussen, David Recker, Krystal Renton, David Russo, Noelle Wald and M. Kelsey Witt, 7-0. Resolution 14-089 issued a two-year probationary administrative contract without tenure to Ms. Kris Young as Director of Technology effective August 11, 2014, 7-0. Resolution 14-090 exercised the option under Section 105c of the State School Aid Act of 1979, as amended by Public Act 300 of 1996, to accept applications for the 2015-2016 school year for an unlimited number of 9th grade students attending districts in another county whose Intermediate School District is contiguous with the Oakland Intermediate School District, for the International Academy East program, 7-0. Resolution 14-091 awarded the Smart Board Widescreen Interactive Whiteboard System and LED Touch TVs to VSC for $185,012.50 from the 2014 Capital Projects Fund, 7-0. Resolution 14-092 awarded Athens High School addition and remodeling work to North American Construction Enterprises (general trades) $483,750.00, Contrast Mechanical (mechanical) $190,000.00, McNulty Electric (electrical) $137,700.00 and Nagle Paving (site work) $72,500.00, total bid $883,950.00, 7-0. Resolution 14-093 awarded food services equipment and installation to Stafford-Smith, Inc. for $90,140.00 from the 2014-2015 Food Services Fund, 7-0. Resolution 14-094 certified Paula Fleming, Todd Miletti, Nancy Philippart and Karl Schmidt as delegates to the MASB 2014 Delegate Assembly, November 6-9, 2014, 7-0. Dr. Machesky reported secure entrances would be completed by October 2014, discussed Larson and Boulan Park roofing and weather concerns, elementary site work and high school renovations, an administrator retreat, and an August 26th staff kick-off at Athens High School. The meeting adjourned at 7:51 p.m.; minutes submitted by Karl D. Schmidt, Secretary.

PERSONNEL. Probationary contracts for 2014-2015 were recommended for Jessica Allio (1.0 FTE English, Troy High), Melissa Batts (2nd grade, Morse), Amy Bauman (2nd grade, Bemis), Erich Beregszaszy (1.0 FTE physics, Athens), Luchi Cacaj (.8 FTE English, Baker), Holly Christopher (.6 FTE science/PE, Boulan Park/Smith), Janelle Cooper (.8 FTE health/PE, Baker/Smith), JoAnne DiGiuseppe (1.0 FTE resource room, Leonard), Caitlin Donovan (2nd grade, Bemis), Jason Garza (1.0 FTE English, Niles Community High School), Letitia Geary (1.0 FTE elementary vocal music, building TBD), Colleen Gumbel (.7 FTE school psychologist, Services Building), Dustin Harnish (1.0 FTE humanities, Baker), Kathryn Kerch (1.0 FTE resource room, Martell), Jared Kowalski (1.0 FTE resource room, Athens), Clayton Lalko (1.0 FTE resource room, Martell), Alexandria Oleksienko (4th grade, Morse), Kyle Omell (1.0 FTE physics, Athens), Jaclynn Parker (1.0 FTE science, Larson), Meghan Parnell (1.0 FTE mathematics, Athens), Michael Reimann (1.0 FTE mathematics, Smith), Margaret Schmidt (1.0 FTE English/ESL, Larson/Smith), Carrie Stein (4th grade, Hamilton), Marc Vickers (1.0 FTE English, International Academy East), Stacey Waldrup (1.0 FTE English, Troy High) and Julie Weatherhead (.5 FTE counselor, International Academy East), each with a biographical sketch of degrees, certification and prior teaching experience.

Mr. Dan House was recommended as Assistant Principal, Troy High School, on a two-year probationary administrative contract without tenure beginning September 3, 2014. He came to Troy School District in 2004 as a long-term guest teacher for American History, became a permanent social studies teacher at Troy High School in 2005, and has been summer school high school principal for the past three years; he holds a bachelor's degree from the University of Michigan (2001) and a master's in Educational Administration from Saginaw Valley State University (2009).

Mr. Jasen Witt, Assistant Superintendent, Human Resources, presented the 2014/2015 teacher staffing update: 44 new TSD teachers, 8 TSD graduates, 27 teachers with education beyond a bachelor's degree, 19 teachers with five or more years of previous teaching experience (7 of these with ten or more), and 185 total years of previous teaching experience as a group. Welcome slides also name Kaitlin Bucchare, Ross Burdette, Aguib Diop, Lauren Field, Taylor Firman, Jaclyn Morrison, Tanya Myre, Kelly Pasternak, Laura Rasmussen, David Recker, Krystal Renton, David Russo, Tammy Shen, Noelle Wald, Lauren Welch, Holly White and M. Kelsey Witt.

CURRICULUM. Anne Mull, Director of Assessment and Instruction, presented a video on the Student Learning Showcase held May 22nd, an event run each May for the past four years; all 12 elementary schools, 4 middle schools and 3 high schools participate with data walls, substitutes were cut to two per building last year, and there are now three rounds of volunteer presentations. School Improvement Roll-Out Sessions in September will gather feedback. Mike Jolly, Director of Athletics and Enrichment, reported on summer 2014 learning offerings and the Summer Success Academy.

Mrs. Jan Keeling and Mr. Mark Dziatczak presented enrollment reported that morning, compared with a year earlier. Elementary, September 3, 2013 then September 2, 2014: Barnard 508 / 481; Bemis 578 / 564; Costello 353 / 334; Hamilton 479 / 456; Hill 321 / 307; Leonard 459 / 456; Martell 469 / 470; Morse 470 / 454; Schroeder 537 / 519; Troy Union 455 / 484; Wass 425 / 425; Wattles 485 / 467; Early Childhood 30 / 29; elementary total 5,569 / 5,446. Middle schools: Baker 725 / 747; Boulan Park 737 / 757; Larson 705 / 690; Smith 637 / 669; total 2,804 / 2,863. High schools: Athens 1,619 / 1,570; Troy 1,986 / 2,047; IAE 476 / 496; NCHS 112 / 114; GROW 24 / 35; total 4,217 / 4,262. Total students 12,590 / 12,571.

BUSINESS. Bids for Troy High School additions and remodeling, reviewed by Mr. Kenneth Miller, Executive Director of Maintenance and Operations, and Mr. Ronald Curtis, Senior Project Manager of Barton Malow, were recommended for award as an expenditure of the 2014 Capital Projects Fund: Brencal Contractors, concrete, $499,000.00; StresCore, Inc., precast structural concrete, $152,900.00; Brazen & Greer, masonry, $433,500.00; Men of Steel, metal, $121,595.00; N.A.C.E., general trades, $497,750.00; LaDuke Roofing, $105,350.00; Contrast Mechanical, mechanical, $536,000.00; Shoreview Electric, electrical, $153,000.00; Hardman, auger cast piles, $130,000.00; total bid $2,629,095.00. Barton Malow Company (26500 American Drive, Southfield, Michigan 48034; p 248.4365000, f 248.436.5001) wrote to Mr. Miller at 1140 Rankin, Troy, MI 48083 on August 28, 2014 regarding the 2014 Bond Program, Series 1, Bid Package 5. The scope is a new four-classroom addition plus Performing Arts and Music storage additions; proposals were received June 26, 2014. The budget for the work is $1,966,125, resulting in an overage of $662,970 recommended to be funded from construction contingency. Only one bid was originally received for concrete and none for site preparation; McCarthy Construction was notified its 7/24/14 concrete bid would not be accepted, the category was broken into sitework/concrete, auger cast piles and precast structural concrete, and rebidding reduced project cost approximately $200,000. The remaining overage is attributed to market increase, auger cast piles not in the original budget, and added mechanical room, storage and stairwell space; the concrete category also includes site preparation for Bid Package 6. Tabulated bids include McCarthy Construction sitework at $801,830.00 with clarifications citing an estimated auger cast pile length of 2610 LF, ADD $65/LF, DEDUCT $7/LF, a rig crew hourly rate of $950/hr and a deduct of $11,500.00 if load testing is not required; also Efficient Design $642,000.00, Nelson Iron Works $149,734.00, E&L Construction $500,600.00, Precision $500,960.00, Esko Roofing $116,000.00, Tri-Star Roofing $116,800.00, National Roofing $125,981.00, Johnson & Wood $611,000.00, Great Lakes Mechanical $722,000.00, McNulty Electric $171,000.00, Metro Electric $234,000.00, Brencal Contractors $616,000.00, Cortis Brothers $782,900.00, Gemelli Concrete LLC $807,000.00, Niemi Corporation $160,400.00 and Berkel & Company Contractors $191,800.00.

Bids for Boulan Park and Larson Middle Schools' additions and remodeling, also reviewed by Mr. Miller and Mr. Curtis, were recommended for award from the 2014 Capital Projects Fund: McCarthy Construction, concrete, $140,560.00; HMC Mason Contractors, masonry, $401,680.00; Men of Steel, metals, $300,000.00; Precision Contracting Group, general trades, $1,520,000.00; Esko Roofing, roofing, $158,000.00; Johnson-Wood, mechanical, $494,000.00; Shoreview Electric, electrical, $294,000.00; Brencal Contractors, sitework, $117,000.00; total bid $3,425,240.00. Barton Malow's August 28, 2014 letter on the 2013 Bond Program, Series 1, Bid Package 6 states proposals were received July 17, 2014 for construction of a new main office addition with a secure entry, that no sitework bids were received on July 17 so that category was rebid with Bid Package 5, and that the budget for these projects is $2,814,450., resulting in an overage of $610,790. to be funded from construction contingency, attributable to the addition of canopies, an increase in square footage and market factors. Other tabulated bids include Gemelli Concrete $184,686.00, Brazen & Greer $435,909.00, Leidal & Hart $450,828.00, Nelson Iron Works $345,000.00, CCC $1,582,000.00, NACE $1,669,102.00, Contrast Mechanical $496,000.00, Ventcon $559,200.00, Great Lakes Mechanical $560,000.00, Ecker Mechanical $608,400.00, Metro Electric Engineering Technologies $297,000.00 and Great Lakes Power & Lighting $322,000.00.

Bid 9791 for science supplies and equipment covered Athens and Troy High Schools and Smith, Boulan Park, Larson, Baker and Niles Middle Schools under the 2014 Bond Project, Series 1. Invitations were sent to 21 potential bidders with 13 responding, none of which were no-bids; proposals were reviewed by Mr. Mark Dziatczak, Assistant Superintendent, Secondary Instruction, Mr. Todd Hensley, Purchasing Supervisor, Ms. Laura Ritter, Science Coordinator, and science teachers Jeff Moore and Jane Moss. Hensley's August 27, 2014 memorandum to Mark Rajter (Purchasing Department, 4400 Livernois, phone 248 823-4091, fax 248 823-4013, cc Pat Orczykowski) recommends awards to A. Daigger & Company $977.75, Arbor Scientific $885.80, Benz Microscope $5,143.50, Carolina Biological $2,545.56, Fisher Scientific $3,928.89, Frey Scientific $6,079.37, Johnson Scientific $6,640.00, Parco Scientific $2,478.00, Sargent Welch $8,034.56, Sirchie Acquisition $212.91 and Vernier Software & Tech. $32,683.18, for a total bid of $69,609.52. Line-item tabulations cover goggles, electronic balances, microscopes, Ohaus triple beam balances, Vernier LabQuest 2 units, dynamics systems, photogates, autoclaves, centrifuges, spectrophotometers and forensic supplies; other bidders included ETA hand2mind and Products Unlimited.

The Board was asked to approve and set the millage rate. Rates are set every June on the best information then known and are therefore estimates, after which the Michigan Department of Treasury requests districts to certify rates on state-approved forms. Because operating Non-Homestead taxable values grew greater than the rate of inflation, it is necessary to amend Form L-4029 to officially set the rate for the 2014 tax year; the suggested resolution directs that the Tax Rate Request Form L-4029 be amended and forwarded to the appropriate tax jurisdictions. The attached Michigan Department of Treasury Form 614 (Rev. 04-14), 2014 Tax Rate Request, must be completed and submitted on or before September 30, 2014 under MCL Sections 211.24e, 211.34 and 211.34d, with penalty for non-filing under MCL Sec 211.119; taxable value is stated as of 5-27-14. Instructions reference MCL 211.36 and 211.37, State Tax Commission Bulletin 3 of 2014, STC Bulletin No. 11 of 1999 as supplemented by letter of 6/7/2000, Form 2166 (L-4034), MCL 380.1211(3) on Supplemental (Hold Harmless) millages, an October 26, 2004 memo to assessors, and the 18 mills levied by districts without a Supplemental millage.

OTHER. Ron Curtis of Barton Malow presented a 2013 Bond Program Series 1 summer 2014 construction update prepared by Barton Malow and TMP. Summer scope comprised, at elementary schools, 14 secure entrance projects, 7 sitework projects and 7 site lighting projects; at middle schools, 2 roofing projects, 1 locker room replacement and 2 secure entrance additions; at high schools, 1 secure entrance and auditorium upgrade project, 1 LGI room renovation and 3 additions; and corridor door replacement at the Niles Continuing Education Center. Scheduled completion dates: secure entrances 09/30/14; Boulan and Larson roofing replacement 08/22/14; bus/parent drop-off modifications 08/15/14; site lighting 08/15/14; Troy Athens HS 08/18/14 thru 12/19/14; Troy HS 08/20/14 thru 08/14/15; Boulan and Larson additions 08/11/14 thru 07/17/15; Troy HS entrance/auditorium 07/21/14 thru 11/3/14. Building-by-building work is listed for Morse, International Academy, Barnard, Wattles, Hill, Costello, Wass, Troy Union, Leonard, Martell, Hamilton, Bemis and Schroeder. Boulan Park and Larson office additions and the Troy High School classroom and storage additions carry an August 2015 completion date, the Troy High School secure entrance a November 2014 date, and the Boulan Park/Larson roofing is marked complete. Upcoming 2015 work: Athens HS mechanical/electrical/plumbing upgrades; Larson and Boulan mechanical/electrical/plumbing upgrades; Hill and Troy Union roofing; International Academy East pool to LGI conversion; Schroeder and Troy Union bus loop and canopies; Smith MS and Niles gym/locker room upgrades; and Larson and Boulan window replacement. Finally, the district reported a successful Opening Day gathering for all staff at Athens High School the previous Tuesday, where the OneTroy concept was unveiled as a renewed commitment to a unified district that values every employee's role, accompanied by a video.
